messages:
mia: Heads-up — seeing sustained spike into the dedicated pool in us-west-2 (dedicated-usw2). Admission controller started returning rate_capped/rejects around 1772501005. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/d/pool/dedicated-usw2

infra-bot: [ALERT] severity=high service=admission reason=capacity_saturation pool=dedicated-usw2 util=99% queue_len=820 p95_queue_ms=6300

raj: Which tenant(s) are spiking? Is this a single-customer hot-spot or cluster-wide surge?

elena: Quick dump from admission logs (tail):
```
2026-03-18T14:24:05Z admission: reject tenant=c-842 reason=pool_capacity_exceeded pool=dedicated-usw2
2026-03-18T14:24:07Z admission: rate_cap_applied tenant=c-842 tokens=1250/sec limit=1000
2026-03-18T14:24:10Z admission: accept tenant=c-137 pool=dedicated-usw2 after_fallback=hosted
```

elena: Looks like tenant c-842 (AcmeAI) is pinned to a model that is saturating the pool: model=gpt-serve-quant-v2, lots of small streaming requests, batch_size=1, sustained QPS.

raj: Oof. Are fairshare weights set? Can we evict or throttle that tenant temporarily?

mia: Current admission policy for the pool:
```yaml
admission_policy:
  type: fairshare
  per_tenant_token_limit: 1000
  burst_budget: 0
  fallback: hosted
```
Per-tenant burst_budget = 0, so once limit hit it's hard cut. That was intentional for predictability but this is too binary for long tails.

tom: Short-term options:
- increase pool capacity (burst up)
- relax per-tenant limit or give c-842 a temporary higher weight
- enable soft-fallback earlier (route heavy traffic to hosted)

elena: I'm going to run the emergency runbook: /runbook scale-dedicated --region=us-west-2 --pool=dedicated-usw2 --add=2xA100 --ttl=30m (adds burst capacity)

infra-bot: runbook:scale-dedicated started by elena. job_id=rb-9812 nodes_added=2 expected_ready=~90s

mia: Also changing admission config to allow small burst_budget on a per-tenant basis so the controller can smooth the spike. Applying change now (will take ~1 min).

elena: Applied temporary policy: per_tenant_token_limit=1200 burst_budget=300 (ttl 20m)

infra-bot: pool=dedicated-usw2 nodes_ready=2 new_util=76% queue_len=48 p95_queue_ms=980

mia: Metrics trending back down: util=68% queue_len=12 p95_queue_ms=180. Accepting again for most tenants.

raj: Good work. For follow-up: we need a couple action items — tweak defaults, add per-tenant burst budgets, and a separate alert for sustained p95_queue_ms > 2s so we can auto-trigger scaling sooner.

tom: I'll open the infra ticket and schedule a short postmortem. INF-3245 created: "adjust fairshare defaults + add per-tenant burst budgets & autoscale triggers". Postmortem meeting set for tomorrow 10:00 PT.

elena: Note for the postmortem: also verify model-pinning visibility in Console (show tenants pinned models + token profiles) so we can detect heavy pinned workloads earlier.

mia: Closing the thread for now — replication/grafana links and logs saved to the incident folder. If anything regresses ping @oncall. :thumbsup:
